== Biography ==

Hugh Glasgow was probably born about 1705. This estimate is reportedly based on an inscription on a Glasgow family gravestone in St Cedma's churchyard, Larne.<ref>[[Space:Chronology_of_the_Glasgow_Family_in_Northern_Ireland_in_Historical_Context|Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context]].</ref>

=== Residence and property in Larne ===

On 10 March 1736, Hugh Glasgow and [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]], both of Larne, County Antrim, received a lease from Alexander, Earl of Antrim. Memorial 63221 was registered on 10 April 1738 at eleven in the morning.<ref name="lease">Registry of Deeds, Dublin, memorial 63221, lease dated 10 March 1736; registered 10 April 1738. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSN1-FXR2 FamilySearch image 542], image group 008088380, volumes 87–88; original image inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The lease covered two tenements already in their possession on the north side of the street in Newtown, Larne. One had a frontage of 23 feet, bounded east by Mr Agnew's tenement and west by Robert Robinson's. The other had a frontage of 32 feet, bounded east by John Boyd's tenement and west by John White's. Both extended backwards 150 feet.<ref name="lease" />

The annual rent was £1 16 shillings sterling, with receiver's fees of two pence per pound. The term began on the preceding 1 November and was measured by the lives of George II, Frederick Prince of Wales and Prince William Augustus Duke of Cumberland, with provision for replacement lives. The named lives were royal family members, not Glasgow children.<ref name="lease" />

The lease witnesses were James Stenhouse of Larne and William Harrison, clerk to Alexander Stewart of Ballylough. Stenhouse and Robert Wilson of Larne, merchant, witnessed the memorial. Stenhouse proved execution at Carrickfergus on 28 March 1738, stating that Alexander Stewart had executed the lease in the Earl's name and that William and Hugh had executed the lease and memorial.<ref name="lease" />

The memorial names no parent, spouse or child of either lessee and states no relationship between them. The later renewal endorsements remain separate research targets.

=== Joint lessors named in a 1757 assignment ===

A deed poll dated 4 June 1757, Matthew Stewart of Carncastle, farmer, to Robert Rainey of Larne, weaver, concerned a conditional assignment for £20 of Stewart's interest in a lease granted by [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]] of Larne. The original memorial does not date their head lease or describe the holding sufficiently to identify it with the 1736 Newtown tenements.<ref name="JointLessors1757">Registry of Deeds, memorial 159181, manuscript pp. 473–474, deed dated 4 June 1757, registered 26 May 1761; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-MJX4 FamilySearch image 257, opening] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJM-MJP6 image 258, continuation], original images inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

The joint names and Larne locality strongly support association with these lessees, but the record names no Glasgow relative or relationship between William and Hugh. Neither Glasgow executed this assignment; its registration in 1761 does not prove that either was then living. The separate 1751 and 1767 endorsements to the 1736 lease remain unexamined and may identify replacement lives.<ref>PRONI D2977/3A/4/81/72A, 1736 William and Hugh Glasgow lease with 1751 and 1767 endorsements; [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/eCatNI_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI eCatalogue], catalogue description only.</ref>

=== Church ===

A family chronology states that Hugh Glasgow became an elder of the Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian congregation in 1741.<ref>[[Space:Chronology_of_the_Glasgow_Family_in_Northern_Ireland_in_Historical_Context|Chronology of the Glasgow Family in Northern Ireland in Historical Context]].</ref>

A nineteenth-century account quoting the Larne Session Book includes Hugh Glasgow among the members of the Session and records that he died on 8 July 1767.<ref name="death">[https://archive.org/stream/christianunitari0003unse/christianunitari0003unse_djvu.txt “Congregational Memoirs—Larne and Kilwaughter,”] ''The Christian Unitarian'', vol. 3 (1864), p. 197. The account quotes the Larne Session Book entry: “Hugh Glasgow … dead July 8, 1767.”</ref>

Hugh therefore died on 8 July 1767, provided that the elder named in the Session Book was the same Hugh Glasgow who held the 1736 Larne lease.<ref name="death" />

== Research Notes ==

=== Possible son John of Larne ===

[[Glasgow-4179|John Glasgow]], who married [[Allan-6611|Rose Allan]] at Larne in 1769, is a possible son, with low confidence. His estimated birth about 1747 fits Hugh's age and Larne household, but the marriage chronology does not name John's father.<ref>Donna Jean Glasgow, [https://web.archive.org/web/20101124184247id_/http://lifesweaving.com/Glasgow/Kilwaughter/Timeline.html Kilwaughter and Larne Glasgow chronology], entry for John Glasgow and Rose Allan's 1769 marriage. The birth estimate of 1745–48 is the compiler's estimate.</ref> The relationship is a working hypothesis and is marked uncertain. [[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]] remains an alternative father. No evidence establishes that Hugh's wife Ann was John's mother.

The Larne memorial gives Hugh's death as 8 July 1767 aged 62 and commemorates members of his family, but does not name John. It has not been established as a complete enumeration of surviving children, so the omission neither proves nor excludes the proposed relationship.<ref>''Armorial Sculptured Stones of the County Antrim'', ''Ulster Journal of Archaeology'', [https://archive.org/stream/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala/ulsterjournalofa06ulstiala_djvu.txt Glasgow stone at Larne], pp. 47–48.</ref> Further tests include the original registers (PRONI MIC/1B/6) and the renewal endorsements to the 1736 lease (PRONI D2977/3A/4/81/72A).


=== Possible duplicate ===

This profile may represent the same person as [[Glasgow-548|Hugh Glasgow (abt.1706-abt.1760)]]. A merger should not be completed until the conflicting death information and the other relationships attached to the two profiles have been examined. The Larne Session Book supports a death date of 8 July 1767 rather than about 1760.<ref name="death" />

=== Possible Dublin baptism ===

A Hugh Glascoe was baptised in Dublin in 1704, the son of William Glascoe and Jone.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FR3H-8L7 FamilySearch record for Hugh Glascoe].</ref>

No evidence currently establishes that the child baptised in Dublin was the later Hugh Glasgow of Larne. The similar name and approximate date are not enough by themselves to identify them as the same person.

=== 1740 Protestant householder ===

A Hugh Glasgow appears in the 1740 list of Protestant householders for Tamlaght O'Crilly Parish.<ref>[https://www.virtualtreasury.ie/item/PRONI-T808-15258 Virtual Treasury of Ireland, PRONI T808/15258, Names of Protestant Householders, 1740].</ref>

The identification is uncertain. The 1736 lease places Hugh Glasgow in Larne, and the church evidence also associates a man of that name with Larne. The Tamlaght O'Crilly entry should therefore remain a possible identification, not a confirmed event in his life.

=== Duneane surname ambiguity ===
The 1740 Duneane return includes Henry Glads. The reading may represent another surname and is not securely Glasgow. It is retained only as east-Antrim surname context and is not evidence that Henry was this Hugh or a relative.<ref>[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740protestantreturnsantrim.pdf Underlying record source: henry glads duneane 1740].</ref>

=== Mortgage with Hugh Shutter, 1749 ===

A mortgage dated 6 November 1749 records William Eakine of Larne conveying Old Town premises as security to Hugh Shutter and Hugh Glasgow. Hugh Glasgow is described as a merchant of Larne and executed the memorial. The underlying lease was dated 11 August 1748.<ref name="HughMortgage1749">Registry of Deeds, memorial 97407, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSH3-7XCG FamilySearch image 449], original manuscript inspected 21 September 2026.</ref>

Place, date and occupation strongly favour this Hugh. The deed establishes a Glasgow–Shutter business association before the reported 1762 marriage of [[Glasgow-1509|James Glasgow]] to Janet Shutter, but names no relationship and proves neither that marriage nor Hugh’s parentage of James or [[Glasgow-4179|John Glasgow]].

== Biography ==

'''Hugh Glasgow''' was a weaver in County Antrim. His birth date is unknown; he was born before about 1802 based on the known ages of his children.

Three original civil marriage registers name children of a father called Hugh Glasgow, weaver:

* [[Glasgow-3957|Mary Glasgow]], who married [[Montgomery-14069|Thomas Montgomery]] on 13 September 1862, expressly named her father as Hugh Glasgow, weaver.<ref name="MaryMarriage1862">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1862/09623/5489617.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], Thomas Montgomery and Mary Glasgow, 13 September 1862.</ref> This parent-child relationship is direct and confident.
* [[Glasgow-4048|Hugh Glasgow]], aged 23 and a weaver of Liminary, married Ann Wilson on 24 December 1852 and named his father as Hugh Glasgow, weaver.<ref name="HughMarriage1852">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1852/09422/5413278.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], Hugh Glasgow and Ann Wilson, 24 December 1852.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-4047|Eliza Glasgow]], aged 21 and of Liminary, married William Montgomery on 21 August 1854 and named her father as Hugh Glasgow, labourer and weaver.<ref name="ElizaMarriage1854">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1854/09463/5428881.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], William Montgomery and Eliza Glasgow, 21 August 1854.</ref>

The matching father name and occupation prove each child's relationship to a Hugh Glasgow. Hugh junior and Eliza also shared the Liminary residence, strongly indicating that they were siblings. Mary may have been their older sister, but her register gives a different residence and the common name does not by itself prove that all three records identify one father.

== Research Notes ==

=== Relationship to Robert Glasgow ===

Hugh is currently attached as an uncertain son of [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]]. That relationship is not proved. Robert's 1851 Glenleslie household contained an unmarried niece Mary Glasgow, aged 34 and a linen weaver.<ref name="Census1851">[https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Dunaghy/Glenleslie/23/ 1851 Census of Ireland], Glenleslie household 23.</ref> She is a strong candidate for the Mary who later named Hugh as her father. If they were the same woman, Hugh was more probably Robert's brother or another collateral relative than his son. No record inspected names Hugh's parents or explicitly calls Hugh and Robert brothers.

== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
{{Occupation|image=Wikimedia_Commons_photos-3.jpg|text=was a farmer}}

'''Robert Glasgow''' was a farmer at '''Glenleslie, Dunaghy, County Antrim'''. His recorded age of seventy-two in the 1851 census places his birth about '''1779'''. The same return gives County Antrim as his birthplace.<ref name="Glenleslie1851">1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, barony of Kilconway, parish of Dunaghy, Glenleslie, household 23. [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Dunaghy/Glenleslie/23/ National Archives of Ireland, legacy household locator]. Detailed transcription: [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf ''1851 Irish Census Returns: comma-delimited transcription''], printed p. 103, Glenleslie household 23. The transcription, including its absent-member and death entries, was examined; the full original return was not re-examined for this revision.</ref>

He married '''Catherine''', whose maiden name has not been established. Their census return gives '''1803''' as the marriage year. Catherine was sixty-eight in 1851, born in County Antrim, and worked at spinning flax.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

=== Household and family in 1851 ===

Robert and Catherine occupied household 23 at Glenleslie. The seven people recorded as present were:<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

All seven were recorded as born in County Antrim. Two further family members were entered as '''absent in America''': '''John Glasgow''', Robert's son, aged forty and a labourer; and '''Samuel Glasgow''', his son, aged thirty and a linen weaver. They should not be counted among the residents physically present at Glenleslie.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

The death section records '''Catherine Hume''', Robert's granddaughter, who died of scarlatina in '''spring 1850''', aged '''three months'''. Her parents are not identified in the entry.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

The census therefore identifies '''Margaret, John and Samuel''' as Robert's children. His will independently identifies Margaret as his daughter and James and Mary Young as Margaret's children. It does not follow that these were his only children.<ref name="RobertWill">Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie, will dated 3 February 1851, proved 13 February 1854; National Archives of Ireland copy, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ8-MQQJ?view=fullText FamilySearch, image 229]. Will details are retained from the earlier research transcription supplied for this profile; the image was not independently re-examined during this revision.</ref>

=== Will and death ===

Robert made his will at '''Glenleslie on 3 February 1851'''. He left his farm, livestock, furniture and farming utensils to his daughter [[Glasgow-3955|Margaret Glasgow]] for life. After her death, the property was to be divided equally between her children '''James Young''' and [[Young-78755|Mary Young]]. The named executors were '''Andrew McCaughey''' and '''John Kirk'''.<ref name="RobertWill" />

The probate notation states that he died '''in or about 1852'''. The will was proved on '''13 February 1854'''. These details support an approximate death in 1852, not an exact death date or a separately verified place of death.<ref name="RobertWill" />

The earlier research also identified a PRONI index entry for Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie among the '''Connor Diocesan Wills, 1854'''. The date of the will, the approximate death year and the probate year are distinct events.<ref name="PRONI1854">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, Name Search, ''Pre-1858 Wills and Admons'', Connor Diocesan Wills: Robert Glasgow, Glenleslie, 1854. [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Name Search]. Entry details retained from the earlier profile's recorded search of 5 August 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

=== Proposed son: Robert Glasgow of Donbought ===

The younger [[Glasgow-1049|Robert Glasgow]], a forty-year-old linen weaver living with his wife Margaret at Donbought in 1851, remains a '''plausible son or close relative'''. The attached father-son relationship should remain '''uncertain''': neither census household states a relationship between the two men.<ref name="Donbought1851">1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, Dunaghy, Donbought, household 16. [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf Detailed comma-delimited transcription], printed p. 100. Compare W. Scott and W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1851censuskilconway.pdf ''1851 Census for some Parishes and Townlands in the Barony of Kilconway, Co. Antrim''], printed pp. 77-78, references 7883-7890. These are transcriptions of the same census, not independent family records.</ref>

The proposed connection rests on compatible ages, the same parish, a possible earlier Doonbought holding and a reported same-name occurrence in the will. None presently identifies the younger Robert as this Robert's son.

'''The 1825 tithe entry.''' W. Macafee's transcription lists '''Robert Glasco''' at '''Doonbought [Dunbught No. 2]''', Dunaghy, in 1825. The compiler standardises the surname as Glasgow. The entry is on printed page 41, compiler's index '''5804'''; that number is not an original property-lot number.<ref name="Tithe1825">W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrimrevisionnamespdf.pdf ''Data from the Tithe Applotment Books covering the Baronies of Cary, Dunluce and Kilconway in North Antrim plus the Barony of N. E. Liberties, Co. Londonderry''], surname order, dated 17 October 2016, printed p. 41, index 5804: Robert Glasco, Doonbought [Dunbught No. 2], Dunaghy, 1825. Transcription, not an inspected original tithe-book image.</ref> This Robert would have been about forty-six, whereas the younger man would have been about fourteen. The Glenleslie farmer is therefore a better chronological candidate for the 1825 entry. However, the entry supplies no age, wife, children or connection to Glenleslie. Identifying him with the tithe occupier does not, by itself, prove that the younger Robert was his son or succeeded to the same holding.

'''The reported will witness.''' The earlier will transcription lists '''Robert Glasgow, John Hamill, Robert Kirk and Thomas Matter''' as witnesses. It does not identify the same-name Robert as the Donbought man or describe him as a son. The original attestation and signature layout should be checked before treating this as an independently identified second Robert; in particular, a testator's signature must not be mistaken for a witness entry. No correction to the earlier transcription is asserted here.<ref name="RobertWill" />

'''The will is not a complete list of children.''' John and Samuel are named as sons in the census but are not among the beneficiaries in the supplied will summary. The absence of the younger Robert from that summary therefore does not disprove the proposed relationship. Equally, an incomplete beneficiary list cannot be used to prove an additional child.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" /><ref name="RobertWill" />

The father-son link could be strengthened by a documented land succession, a church entry, or an independently established relationship between the younger Robert and one of this man's proved children. A direct statement is not the only possible route to a conclusion, but the present indirect evidence does not yet distinguish a son from another relative or namesake.

=== Margaret and the Glenleslie holding ===

The Dunaghy index to Griffith's Valuation lists '''Margaret Glasgow at Glenleslie''' and, separately, '''Robert Glasgow at Doonbought'''.<ref name="GriffithDunaghy">[https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/dunaghy.php Fáilte Romhat, Griffith's Valuation index, Dunaghy parish, County Antrim], entries for Margaret Glasgow, Glenleslie, and Robert Glasgow, Doonbought. Name-and-townland index; original valuation pages, plot references and revision entries have not been inspected.</ref> The Margaret entry is consistent with the will's provision for his daughter, but her identity and the precise holding remain to be established. This is a possible continuation of the '''Glenleslie''' farm, not proof of father-son succession at '''Doonbought'''.

=== Marriage and age discrepancy ===

Margaret's census age of fifty suggests a birth about 1800 or 1801, slightly before Robert and Catherine's reported marriage in 1803. Either age or marriage year may be inaccurate, or there may be an explanation not recorded in the surviving evidence. The discrepancy remains unresolved; no earlier marriage or different mother has been established.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

=== Identification of the emigrant sons ===

The census establishes that Robert had sons John and Samuel in America in 1851; it does not establish their later residences, wives or children. The earlier attachment of [[Glasgow-3140|John Glasgow]] to the Elizabeth Fee and County Armagh family remains unproved. Robert's absent son John must also be distinguished from the forty-year-old nephew in [[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]]'s nearby household 21: that nephew was present at Glenleslie, was a linen weaver and had married in 1839.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

[[Glasgow-1053|Margaret (Glasgow) Winters]], associated with a Canadian family, has not been identified with Robert's unmarried daughter at Glenleslie. Their profiles should not be merged on the strength of their common name.

=== Mary Glasgow, niece, and the Hugh Glasgow lead ===

The thirty-four-year-old niece may be [[Glasgow-3957|Mary (Glasgow) Montgomery]]. The earlier civil-register research records that Mary's marriage to Thomas Montgomery on '''13 September 1862''' named her father as '''Hugh Glasgow, weaver'''. Her death on '''22 March 1898''' gives an age consistent with birth about 1818, close to the census niece's estimated birth about 1816 or 1817.<ref name="MaryMarriage1862">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Thomas Montgomery and Mary Glasgow, 13 September 1862: [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1862/09623/5489617.pdf register image]. Record details retained from the earlier profile's research.</ref><ref name="MaryDeath1898">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, Mary Montgomery, 22 March 1898: [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1898/05842/4654852.pdf register image]. Record details retained from the earlier profile's research.</ref>

This remains an identification to test, not proof that Hugh was Robert's brother. The census niece relationship does not identify the connecting parent, and a relationship through Catherine must also be considered.

A Hugh Glasgow, weaver, was also named as father in the Liminary-associated marriages of '''Hugh Glasgow and Ann Wilson, 24 December 1852''', and '''Eliza Glasgow and William Montgomery, 21 August 1854'''. Mary may belong to that family, but the common paternal name and occupation do not establish the connection.<ref name="HughMarriage1852">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Hugh Glasgow and Ann Wilson, 24 December 1852: [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1852/09422/5413278.pdf register image]. Earlier research comparison.</ref><ref name="ElizaMarriage1854">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, William Montgomery and Eliza Glasgow, 21 August 1854: [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1854/09463/5428881.pdf register image]. Earlier research comparison.</ref>

=== Robert's parents and earlier hypotheses ===

'''Robert's parents remain unidentified.''' The County Antrim birthplace comes from his census return; a previously reported County Tyrone birthplace has no supporting source in this profile.<ref name="Glenleslie1851" />

[[Glasgow-3902|Adam Glasgow]] and Rose of Inishrush were previously suggested as his parents, but the attachment is not retained. Adam's reported birth about 1758 makes the paternal chronology possible, while Rose's reported birth about 1767 would make her about twelve at Robert's birth. That is a serious chronological difficulty, not evidence of maternity. Their documented County Londonderry association also supplies no link to Robert's County Antrim family.

The proposal drew on the incomplete family named on Adam and Rose's gravestone and a notice describing Nancy Glasgow as Adam's '''sixth daughter'''. Those sources show that some of Adam's children are not named on the stone; neither identifies Robert as one of them.<ref name="AdamGrave">[https://www.oneirishrover.com/tamlaght-graveyard/ ''Tamlaght O'Crilly Lower Graveyard''], Glasgow gravestone transcription and photograph naming Rose, wife of Adam Glasgow; Adam; daughter Eliza; son James; and grandson William. Source retained from the earlier research.</ref><ref name="NancyMarriage">[https://cotyrone.com/~inthenews/marriages-notices-1840-42/ ''Marriage Notices 1840-42''], notice published 29 January 1842: John Kyle of Tyanee married Nancy, sixth daughter of Adam Glasgow of Inishrush, on 14 January 1842. Source retained from the earlier research.</ref>

[[Glasgow-1022|John Glasgow]] of Glenleslie was another proposed father. No record establishes that relationship. Robert's birth also precedes John and Rose Alexander's reported 1791 marriage, although that alone would not exclude an earlier marriage. Household proximity is not sufficient evidence of parentage.

=== Namesakes and other unproved connections ===

* '''Coltrim:''' [[Glasgow-3941|Robert Glasgow of Coltrim]] is separately associated with Coltrim, Lissan, between 1820 and 1831. No inspected record bridges him to Robert and Catherine at Glenleslie.
* '''Lisnagaver:''' the Robert Glasgow in the 1834 Rasharkin tithe material has not been identified with this man. The older John and Samuel of Lisnagaver must not be substituted for Robert's much younger sons of those names.
* '''Gortereghy:''' this man, whose death is placed about 1852, cannot simply be treated as the later occupier. [[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]], whose 1866 marriage names his father as Alexander, is the stronger existing candidate for the later Lisnagaver-Gortereghy identity.<ref name="Robert938Marriage">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Robert Glasgow and Jane Graham, 1866: [https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/images/marriage_returns/marriages_1866/11531/8240963.pdf register image]. Identification comparison retained from earlier research.</ref>
* '''Possible duplicate:''' [[Glasgow-2963|Robert Glasgow]], born about 1780 and attached to [[Glasgow-1142|James Glasgow]] and [[Simpson-19200|Jean Simpson]], has not been connected to Catherine or the Glenleslie household. A merge is not supported at present.

Earlier possibilities involving [[Glasgow-1023|Thomas Glasgow]], born about 1725; [[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]], born about 1690; [[Glasgow-548|Hugh Glasgow]], born about 1706; and [[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]], born about 1710, remain unconnected hypotheses. Previously reported FamilyTreeDNA relationship-distance figures, RDist 3 and GDist 6, do not establish a documentary chain to any particular couple.

The Blair extracts of the ''Belfast Newsletter'' list William, John, James and Robert Glasgow on 7 April 1772. These are earlier surname occurrences, not evidence of this Robert's parentage.<ref name="Belfast1772">[https://www.kinsleuth.com/belnews/1770-1779.htm ''Blair Extracts from the Belfast Newsletter, 1770-1779''], 7 April 1772, p. 3. Source retained from the earlier profile.</ref>

=== Relationship assessment ===

The recorded household and the supplied will transcription support Catherine as Robert's wife; Margaret, John and Samuel as his children; Mary and James Young as Margaret's children and his grandchildren; Mary Glasgow as his niece; and Catherine Hume as his granddaughter through an unidentified parent. Identification of James Young with [[Young-23682|James Young]] remains unproved. The proposed younger son [[Glasgow-1049|Robert Glasgow]], Robert's own parents and the wider family links remain uncertain.

'''Mary Glasgow''' was born about 1818 in County Antrim, Ireland. She was a
linen weaver and the daughter of '''Hugh Glasgow''', also a weaver. No compatible
WikiTree profile has yet been identified for Hugh.

Mary married Thomas Montgomery on 13 September 1862. The civil register
describes her as of full age and unmarried and names her father as Hugh Glasgow,
weaver.<ref name="Marriage1862">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1862/09623/5489617.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register], Ballymena district, Thomas Montgomery and Mary Glasgow, 13 September 1862.</ref>

Mary died at Crankill on 22 March 1898, aged seventy-nine. Her son John
Montgomery was present at the death.<ref name="Death1898">[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1898/05842/4654852.pdf General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register], Ballymena district, Mary Montgomery, 22 March 1898.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
Mary is probably the unmarried thirty-four-year-old linen weaver recorded as
The niece of [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow]] at Glenleslie in 1851.<ref>[https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/census-record/#census_year=1851&surname__icontains=Glasgow&county=Antrim&limit=30&id=31235 1851 Census of Ireland], Glenleslie household 23.</ref> If the identification is correct, Mary's father Hugh was probably Robert's brother. The match is strong but still indirect.

[[Glasgow-3956|Joseph Glasgow]] was previously attached as Mary's father through
a misreading of the marriage register. The original certificate clearly names
her father as Hugh Glasgow, weaver, so Joseph was detached.

Glasgow-3904.public_addition_wikitext:
=== Prescott sibling family reviewed 18 October 2026 ===
John Glasgow, Prescott watchmaker with wife Jane in deed B13, is selected as Robert [[Glasgow-4150]]’s brother at 98% subjective confidence. Robert’s 1849 will gives brother John one sixth. John and Jane’s 1856 deed transfers an undivided one sixth of the same Dibble Street lots to Samuel, who is another will-named brother. The exact locality, buyer, parcels and fraction identify the grantor strongly; B13 does not itself expressly call John Robert’s brother. John’s birth, death and parents are not named, and his identity with an existing John profile is unresolved.

Mary Black, formerly Mary Glasgow, is Robert’s sister at 99% subjective confidence: C298 expressly states that relationship and traces her six children’s interests to Robert’s will, which names his sister Mary. Her children were John Black and Rose Ann Black of Drumoolish, Jane Miller and Agnes Black of Newburgh, Thomasina Montgomery of Legrand, Iowa, and Elizabeth Black, formerly of Newburgh. John’s wife Martha, Jane’s husband Robert Miller and Thomasina’s husband Mathew Montgomery also joined. Elizabeth, not Mary, is expressly deceased unmarried and intestate; her five siblings convey her share as heirs. Mary’s own birth, death, residence and husband’s forename remain unknown.

Extend the existing Alexander [[Glasgow-3904]] father hypothesis to John and Mary at 27%, uncertain, conditional on their documented membership in the Prescott sibling family. Thomas-987 and Daniel-3896 already carry this father, and Samuel-4010 and Robert-4150 already have the same selected uncertain hypothesis. Its basis remains the single late descendant tradition naming Alexander as Thomas’s father, with compatible generation and sibling inference. The original will and deeds name no parent. These two extensions supply no independent parent testimony and do not raise the existing estimate; no mother is selected.

These are two previously unstructured record accounts recovered from evidence already researched in September, not two newly discovered sources or two proven additional distinct people. John retains six unselected compatible or weak existing-profile comparisons; later residence, spouse or death elsewhere is not by itself an exclusion of a possible migrant. No Mary Black/Glasgow match is established in the bounded local historical catalogue check. Both accounts remain on identity hold before any new WikiTree profile creation. Record dates are not birth dates.

Resolve John against the retained profile candidates using Jane, his watchmaking trade and the exact Prescott household. Compare the six Black children’s Irish and North American records for an identification of Mary and her husband. A contemporary source naming a parent remains the decisive question for Alexander; the later accounts cannot be counted twice.<ref name="PrescottSiblingReview18Oct2026">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S Robert Glasgow’s will, B12, 9 October 1849, registered 13 November 1856; volume B, pp. 9–10, images 35–36]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 John and Jane Glasgow to Samuel, B13, 30 October 1856, registered 13 November 1856; volume B, pp. 10–11, image 36]; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQTY-K Mary Black’s children to Mary Eno Glasgow, C298, 15 September 1869, registered 1 July 1870; volume C, pp. 477–482, images 277–280]. The relationship clauses were reread 18 October 2026; later C298 execution details reuse the original inspection of 13 September 2026.</ref>

Glasgow-4150.remote_wikitext: {{Estimated Date}} [[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] == Biography == '''Robert Glasgow''' was an early shipbuilder at Prescott, Upper Canada, later Canada West. Prescott heritage material identifies him as the builder of the Centre Street house now known as Glasgow House.Town of Prescott, [https://www.prescott.ca/media/3dtiztjk/council-agenda-june-16-2025.pdf ''Council Agenda, 16 June 2025''], heritage-designation material for 388 Centre Street, “Glasgow House.” A later property history dates the building to about 1835.Theresa Taylor, [https://www.theresataylor.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Auction-all-for-others-Brockville-Recorder.pdf “Auction all for others,”] ''Brockville Recorder & Times'', 22 February 2017. Robert made his will on 9 October 1849. The registered copy divides his estate into six shares: one each for his brothers Daniel, [[Glasgow-4010|Samuel]], John and Thomas Glasgow, one collectively for the children of his brother James, and one for his sister Mary Glasgow.FamilySearch, ''Land records of Grenville County, 1822–1955'', film 008200419, image 35, registered copy of the will of Robert Glasgow of Prescott, dated October 1849 and registered in 1856, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S image 3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S]; original image inspected 8 September 2026. The explicit sibling language makes Samuel Robert's brother, not his son. The later statement that Robert left the house to six “children” and that a son Samuel acquired the other shares appears to have misread the six-share title chain. Local history reports that Robert died at Prescott in 1856. The 1856 date is compatible with an 1849 will: 1849 is the date on which the will was made, while 1856 is the reported death and registration period. == Research Notes == === The 1842 census lead === A modern index reports a Robert Glasgow in Augusta in the 1842 Canada West census. The image formerly cited for that claim, frame 004569584_00050, was inspected at full resolution and contains no readable Robert Glasgow entry.Library and Archives Canada, [https://central.bac-lac.gc.ca/.item/?app=Census1842&op=img&id=004569584_00050 1842 Census of Canada West, image 004569584_00050], inspected 13 August 2026. It is not used here as evidence for Robert's identity. === Family interpretation === The will's named beneficiaries are Robert's siblings and the children of one brother. It does not name Robert's parents, spouse or children. The 30 July 1861 conveyance, B465, identifies the will’s Daniel as the Kilrea watchmaker and Thomas as the Lisnagaver farmer, with wives Margaret and Mary Anne. This establishes the Irish sibling identities when read with the will; it does not name their parents or identify Alexander of Lisnagaver as another brother.[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWB8-D Prescott land register, volume B, memorial 465, pp.397–398, DGS 008200419, images 240–241]. The 1861 deed identifies the brothers as [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel of Kilrea]] and [[Glasgow-987|Thomas of Lisnagaver]]. The original 15 September 1869 deed, C298, identifies the sister as Mary Black, formerly Glasgow, and names six children, including John and Rose Ann Black of Drumoolish.[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQTY-K Prescott land register, volume C, memorial 298, pp.476–482, DGS 008200420, images 277–280]. John of Prescott, watchmaker, remains an unassigned profile identity. James the Prescott carpenter is a property-based comparison for brother James, but their identity is not yet proved; the will does not say James was deceased. Robert's actual birthplace is unknown. His birth is estimated only far enough before about 1835 for him to have worked as a shipbuilder and built the house. His brother Samuel was recorded as Irish-born in the original 1851 Prescott census.Library and Archives Canada, [https://central.bac-lac.gc.ca/.item/?app=Census1851&op=img&id=e002351566 1851 Census of Canada West, Prescott, page 31, lines 11–18, image e002351566], Samuel Glasgow household. Ireland is therefore a usable uncertain creation-field location from Robert's documented immediate-family context; it is not a statement that Robert's birthplace has been found. Prescott should be entered as an uncertain death place from the local history, not as a birthplace. === Duplicate audit === The local One Tree export, current project index and live WikiTree name results were reviewed in August and September 2026. No compatible Prescott shipbuilder profile was found. [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie]], [[Glasgow-1171|Robert Glasgow of New York]], [[Glasgow-1983|Robert Glasgow of South Carolina]], [[Glasgow-1189|Robert Glasgow of Ohio]] and [[Glasgow-2769|Robert Glasgow of Tennessee]] have incompatible documented lives. Create Robert unconnected; the sibling link to Samuel can be expressed in the biographies until their parents are identified. == Sources ==

== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''' lived in Irvine, Ayrshire, Scotland. He was named as the father of the following children in the Irvine parish registers:

* [[Glasgow-4112|Janet Glasgow]], baptised 1703
* [[Glasgow-4119|Margaret Glasgow]], baptised 1708
* [[Glasgow-4100|James Glasgow]], baptised 19 August 1711
* [[Glasgow-4102|Mary Glasgow]], baptised 1713
* [[Glasgow-2474|Robert Glasgow]], baptised 1716
* [[Glasgow-3080|William Glasgow]]

His wife was '''Isabell Kyle''', whose surname also appears in the baptism records as '''Kelle''', '''Kylle''' and '''Keill'''; she was named as the mother in the same records.<ref>Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', Irvine Old Parish Registers, Ayrshire; the individual baptism entries are cited on each child's profile.</ref><ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTV2-YVQ John Glasgow in entry for Robert Glasgow], 1716.</ref>

He was potentially related to [[Glasgow-1406|Michael Glasgow (bef.1680-)]] of the same Ayrshire branch.

== Research Notes ==

The children are linked by the recurring father John Glasgow and mother Isabell in the Irvine registers. The records do not give John's own parents, birth or death.

The Irvine registers also record a John Glasgow with Agnes Martine (baptism 08 October 1693); no link to this John has been established.

The reproduced Third Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records Robert Elder, full-age bachelor labourer of Ballymoney, marrying Jane Adams McCaughey, full-age spinster of Garvaghey, on 13 July 1887. new_people.name: Thomas Glasgow of Quothquan, 1527/28
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
7 February 1527/28: Thomas Gleschow is listed with Quothquan tenants fined for nonappearance in a case concerning breach of the lord’s judicial prohibition (called his “fence” in the text). The heading says 1527; Dickinson’s Appendix B assigns the court to 1527/28.<ref>William Croft Dickinson (ed.), Court Book of the Barony of Carnwath 1523–1542 (1937), printed pp.64–65, index p.217; Appendix B p.cxx; PDF 193–194; https://deriv.nls.uk/dcn23/1271/7974/127179749.23.pdf#page=193. Printed edition inspected 15 October 2026; original manuscript uninspected.</ref>

The remaining Thomas passages belong to five court meetings in all: 7 and 23 February 1527/28, 10 March 1527/28, 27 March 1528 and 20 May 1528. The February and 10 March meetings are entered twice. At the 27 March court Thomas is included in the tenant group adjudged to have broken two judicial prohibitions: cultivating Newmains while restricted and paying rents out despite an arrestment. Fines and imprisonment for a year at the lord’s will were decreed; actual imprisonment is not established. These proceedings name no Glasgow relative.<ref>Dickinson (1937), printed pp.64–70,79–88; Appendix B p.cxx; PDF193–199,208–217,125; https://deriv.nls.uk/dcn23/1271/7974/127179749.23.pdf#page=214. Printed edition inspected 15 October 2026; original manuscript uninspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The tenant list begins “in Quodquen” on p.64; Thomas Gleschow falls before the separate Carswell names on p.65. This supports Quothquan itself, not merely the broad barony. John and Thomas form a plausible local family group, with their degree of kinship unknown. [[Glasgow-1095|John Glasgow]] is the leading possible existing-profile comparison for the Quothquan John, not a proved identification or parent of Thomas.



The five meetings are treated as one tenant’s career. The rolls do not identify his exact individual holding or establish that he inherited from John. Leases and tenancy succession might identify kin. No compatible existing profile was found in the bounded duplicate audit; the Dublin 1725 and Calton 1886 Thomas accounts have incompatible chronologies.

== Sources ==
<references />
new_people.assessment: No compatible early Thomas profile was found in the inherited complete Thomas+Glasgow result review. The actual dossiers for Thomas-3943 (Dublin death 1725) and Thomas-3176 (Calton death 1886) cannot represent a living adult in 1528; no unsupported estimated birthday is needed for those exclusions. Consolidate the five dated court meetings and repeated entries as one Quothquan tenant, not one person per page. A full sourced draft is supplied from the visually verified printed court book; John is a possible local relative with no chosen degree, and no descent to the seventeenth-century Quothquan weaver is asserted.

new_people.name: Sarah Glasgow, daughter of William of Currituck
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

Sarah Glasgow was a daughter of [[Glasgow-428|William Glasgow]] of Currituck, North Carolina. Her father named her in his will of 30 September 1746, proved 7 April 1747.<ref name="William1746">[https://www.ncgenweb.us/currituck/wills/glasgowwilliam1746.html William Glasgow will, 30 September 1746; proved 7 April 1747, North Carolina State Archives MARS 12.96.1.805; NCGenWeb published transcription checked 17 October 2026].</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Her mother, exact dates and later identity remain unknown. The will names her paternal siblings Caleb, Abiah and Elizabeth; the identification of the adult Caleb profiles remains probable. The unnamed grandfather and the wife’s unborn child are not assigned modern identities. The contingent land interest and cattle in a mark given by an unnamed grandfather belong to Sarah’s bequest; the will does not name that grandfather. The account is based on the checked published transcription; the manuscript has not been newly inspected.

Her later life is untraced; the supplied draft preserves her one family role without a mother assignment. Fresh Sarah/Glasgow surname-variant searches found no compatible Glasgow/Glasco/Glascoe historical account. Do not conflate Sarah with Lowdenner, Abiah, Elizabeth or the unborn child, or infer her mother from Susanah's status as testator's wife. new_people.name: Walter Glasgow of Leithford, buried in 1647
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
Walter Glasgow was indexed as buried on 4 June 1647 in the Kirknewton/East Calder register, with residence Leithford and next of kin William Glasgow, relationship “Son to”. The original is not inspected; burial is not an exact death date.<ref>Findmypast/SGS, Walter Glasgow, burial 4 June 1647, Leithford; OPR 689/20; https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBUR%2F1625437.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The burial precedes both proposed 23 September 1647/1649 baptism dates for Glasgow-1554. It cannot be assigned to that later-born/baptised child on the current chronology. Reuse of the name within one family is possible, but the adult father’s identity and relationship between the two Walters remain unproved.
Inspect OPR 689/20 for the burial and both baptism readings; verify any year heading or transcription error before treating the two Walters as proved siblings or creating a new person.

=== Preferred father and the two Walters — 17 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-1087|William Glasgow]] is the selected probable father, at 68% subjective confidence. The transcript’s explicit William father role is assessed at 98%; the same-father Leithford household comparison with the later [[Glasgow-1554|Walter]] is 84%. The 68% identification with the Mid Calder man is a separate, weaker inference; these figures are not independent probabilities. No mother is assigned.

The burial and later baptism name William and the exact Leithford residence, with the same register reference. The later baptism follows the burial under either disputed year, consistent with reuse of a dead child’s name. Another William of Leithford remains the principal alternative; William-3517 and William-1556 lack this local household chain, while the older Leith mealmaker William-3075 is weaker geographically, not excluded solely because he died before the burial.

The two Walters remain separate record accounts pending original-year verification. This source-verification HOLD remains in force; no live creation, merge, exact death date or infant age follows.<ref>Findmypast/SGS, Walter Glasgow burial, 4 June 1647, Leithford, OPR 689/20, https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBUR%2F1625437; Walter Glasgow baptism indexed 23 September 1647, same residence/reference, https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F4473489. Supplied ScotlandsPeople OPR 690/10/19 and FamilySearch https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-FWL instead give 23 September 1649. William’s Mid Calder christening, 24 December 1609, OPR 694/10/15: https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1B2-3LV. Maintained provider readings reused; originals not inspected in this review.</ref>

== Sources ==

The later Walter’s baptism names William at the same Leithford residence and register, supporting one household and reuse of the name after the June 1647 burial. new_people.name: Alexander Elder
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

The published headstone transcription for Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church records a memorial erected by Alexander Elder of Gortrickey to his father Robert Elder, his mother Jane, and his sisters and brothers. It also records Alexander Elder's death on 5 January 1943.<ref>Rasharkin Second Presbyterian Church headstones; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/graveyard.html; . This is a new direct memorial transcription for the catalogue's parentage study, not a Glasgow record and not proof that the Elder family was related to Alexander Glasgow. Its value is locality context: Gortrickey/Gortereghy is the townland where the Glasgow family appears in the 1837–1838 Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism entries. The memorial supplies a named Elder household for future comparison with the later Robert Elder who occupied Alexander Glasgow's former Lisnagaver lot; identity between those Elder references remains unproved.</ref>

A 2007 RootsChat research post reproduces a 18 June 1908 Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage entry for Alexander Elder, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, whose father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer. Alexander married Mary Anderson, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, daughter of Neil Anderson; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Margaret Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . The entry is not yet an inspected original, so it is a secondary-source lead rather than final evidence. It is nevertheless a new, specific parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and gives a testable route for determining whether the Alexander Elder on the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial was a son of the Robert Elder who later occupied Alexander Glasgow's Lisnagaver lot. That identity chain remains unproved.</ref>

The inspected original 1911 Gortereghy census return records Alexander Elder, aged 40, as head, Mary Elder, aged 44, as wife, Robert Elder, aged 34, as brother, and Margaret Elder, aged 25, as sister (Form A, official index house 37, nai001390156, rows 1–4). These stated relationships support comparison with the 1901 household, the 1908 marriage lead and the Rasharkin Second Presbyterian memorial; identification with existing profiles remains qualified.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Alexander Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390156.pdf; Form A; official index house 37; rows 1–4. Original register or Form A inspected on 30 September 2026; source-specific image and entry references supplied. Profile identities and cross-record continuity remain qualified where stated.</ref>

The original 1901 Gortereghy return records Robert Elder, 65, widowed farmer, with Alex 27 and Robert 20 as sons and Eliza 22 and Margaretta 14 as daughters. The 1911 Alexander/Mary household explicitly records Robert as Alexander’s brother and Margaret as his sister. The combined names and locality strongly support continuity, with age differences retained. Robert [[Elder-7144]] remains a qualified father identity; Robert/Mary Glasgow’s Gortahar household is separate.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Robert Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298460.pdf; Form A; official index house 42; rows 1–5; 1911 Gortereghy, Alexander Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390156.pdf; Form A; official index house 37; rows 1–4. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Identity revalidation, 17 October 2026: The original 1901 Alex is explicitly Robert’s son; the 1911 return names brother Robert and sister Margaret. Together with the 1908 Alexander/Mary Anderson marriage extract, these support one sibling family. Retain the actual age differences. Use the same qualified Elder-7144 father hypothesis for Alexander and proved siblings; mother Jane on the memorial is separately evidenced, while Jane Calderwood remains a comparison. No matching Alexander profile was established in full same-name and father-filtered searches.

== Biography ==

The same reproduced Second Portglenone Presbyterian marriage list records Neal Anderson, full-age bachelor farmer of Gortreaghy, marrying Sarah Elder, full-age spinster of Gortreaghy, on 28 September 1893. Sarah's father is recorded as Robert Elder, farmer; witnesses were Robert Anderson and Nancy Elder.<ref>RootsChat, Elder, Murdoch & McMeekin Families; https://www.rootschat.com/forum/index.php?topic=214109.0; . This is a new parent-bearing record for the Gortreaghy Elder household and is consistent with the 1908 entry naming Alexander Elder as a son of a Robert Elder, but the shared father's identity and any connection to Robert Elder, husband of Mary Glasgow, remain unproved until the original register is inspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Identity revalidation, 17 October 2026: Sarah is explicitly the wife named in Anderson-47669's citation to the marriage of 28 September 1893, but no separate compatible Sarah Elder profile was identified in the live cohort. The nearby County Antrim Sarah Elder-6116 was born in 1899, after the marriage.

== Biography ==

The same 1911 Gortereghy browse lists two further Elder households not currently represented in the catalogue: Joseph Elder, aged 79, with Ellen Elder, aged 38, recorded as his niece, and William Elder, aged 40, with Elizabeth Elder, aged 50, recorded as his sister. This demonstrates that Gortereghy contained several distinct Elder households at the same time.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Joseph Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390154.pdf; Form A; official index/printed house 36; rows 1–2; 1911 Gortereghy, William Elder household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390136.pdf; Form A; official index house 27; rows 1–2. Global near-age Elder-6578 belongs to a Utah family as a daughter of Claybourne and Mary Pratt, with a different family and locality.

new_people.name: Caroline McCaughern
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

The 1911 Gortereghy census browse records Sarah McCaughern, aged 82, as head of household with Matilda Mulholland, 52, and Caroline McCaughern, 47, recorded as daughters; Sara Jane McCaughern, 45, and Jas Alex McCaughern, 43, are also listed as children, with Geo Mulholland, 14, as grandson. It confirms a substantial McCaughern household in the same townland as the Elder and Glasgow-associated records, but it does not identify Sarah's husband, parents or relationship to Mary Glasgow.<ref>1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf; Form A; official index house 26; rows 1–6. Original register or Form A inspected on 30 September 2026; source-specific image and entry references supplied. Profile identities and cross-record continuity remain qualified where stated.</ref>

The original 1901 and 1911 returns establish continuity of Sarah McCaughern’s Gortereghy family. Sarah was a Derry-born widow aged 72/82; Caroline, Sarah J/Sara Jane, James A/Jas Alex, Matilda and grandson George occur in both returns. Elizabeth, 32, is also a daughter in 1901. Sarah [[Dysart-1893]], married in 1851 to Gortereghy farmer John McCaughern, remains the strongest mother identity, but neither census names her deceased husband or maiden surname.<ref>1901 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai000298441.pdf; Form A; official index house 18; rows 1–7; 1911 Gortereghy, Sarah McCaughern household; https://api-census.nationalarchives.ie/census/image/nai001390134.pdf; Form A; official index house 26; rows 1–6; Rasharkin Presbyterian civil marriage register 1851; https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1851/09402/5405894.pdf; PDF page 1; entry 28. Inspected original record; profile identity remains qualified where stated.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Identity revalidation, 17 October 2026: Caroline McCaughern/McCarnagh searches returned zero results. McCaughan returned only other given-name or later-generation variants, without a compatible Caroline born about 1864 and daughter of Sarah. No existing profile was identified within this explicit search scope. The original 1901/1911 returns establish the household’s continuity. Carry Dysart-1893 as the qualified mother identity and John McCaughern-23 as the corresponding uncertain father hypothesis for proved siblings. George’s particular mother remains unproved.

new_people.name: Hugh Macaw
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

A fresh audit of the surviving Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription located a second parent-bearing McCaughern/Macaw household at the target townland. Hugh Macaw was born 3 February 1839 and baptised 3 March 1839 as the son of William and Mary Kilpatrick, resident at Lisnagaver (entry 125).<ref>Rasharkin Presbyterian baptisms, entries 125 and 204; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html; . The same register records Jane Matilda Macaw, born 26 July 1843 and baptised 14 January 1844, as the daughter of William and Mary Kilpatrick at Granagh (entry 204). Named transcription reread 30 September 2026; originalmanuscriptuninspected.</ref>

Rereading Rasharkin baptism transcription entry 125 gives Hugh Macaw’s birth as 3 February 1839, replacing the maintained 5 February wording. His baptism remains 3 March 1839; original manuscript inspection is required before treating the corrected transcription as a final date.<ref>Rasharkin Presbyterian baptism transcription; https://genealogy.torrens.org/BannValley/church/RasharkinP/Baptisms_1834.html; transcription entries 125 and 204; original MIC/1P/292 uninspected. Named transcription reread; original manuscript uninspected.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Identity revalidation, 17 October 2026: No compatible infant profile was identified through Hugh Macaw/McCaw/McCaughan searches. McCaw-10 represents the father of John, born about 1833. McCaw-233 represents an adult born about 1812 and father of Eliza, born about 1832. These are older generations, not the 1839 infant. The freshly inspected published baptism transcription, row 125, gives birth on 3 February 1839 and baptism on 3 March, whereas the maintained handoff gave 5 February. The original image is still needed to settle the date. Consolidate Hugh and Jane Matilda with the same named parental couple. Rereading the transcription gives 3 February 1839, with the manuscript still uninspected. Parent profile identities remain uncertain; later spouses alone do not exclude an earlier family.

new_people.name: Nicholas Glasco / Glascoe
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Nicholas Glasco is named in a 20 June 1746 report in the ''Weekly Worcester Journal'' among officers in the rebel army committed to New Gaol, Southwark. The notice lists him between John Duncan and Alexander M'Laughlan. It gives no rank for Nicholas individually and does not state a conviction, birthplace, residence, relatives, occupation, or dates of birth or death.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1214317653/ ''Weekly Worcester Journal'', 20 June 1746, p.4], original roster inspected 4 October 2026. Date follows provider metadata; masthead date has not been separately checked.</ref>


The 27 and 28 June reports describe Nicholas Glascoe as a self-styled major and allege a role in the attack on the Hazard sloop. These are allegations, not a finding of guilt.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/394536822/ The Derby Mercury, 1746-06-27, p.1], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404059808/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1746-06-28, p.1], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

An August report lists Nicholas among persons indicted for high treason, while the 7 November paper announces the pending trial.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404060798/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1746-08-23, p.2], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/394542827/ The Derby Mercury, 1746-11-07, p.3], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

The 8 and 17 November reports say he was acquitted, with defence evidence identifying him as a French native born at Saint-Germain-en-Laye and a lieutenant in Dillon’s Regiment. They report an order to detain him as a French prisoner. The Caledonian account also mentions a Not Guilty verdict and removal of his bolts; the saved excerpt stops before the full cartel articles. These reports require comparison with the underlying legal and military records.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404061824/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1746-11-08, p.3], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/394462695/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1746-11-17, p.2], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

In May 1747 a notice names Mr Glascoe as major in Lord Ogilvy’s new regiment. Nicholas is a probable contextual candidate, but the missing forename and unproved continuity prevent a firm identification.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/404076485/ The Newcastle Weekly Courant, 1747-05-09, p.1], original passage visually inspected 5 October 2026; issue metadata supplied by Newspapers.com.</ref>

No parents, spouse, children, birth date, death date or Irish origin is established.

Further original issues preserve June rosters, indictment reprints and Dutch reports, along with acquittal reports containing translated cartel articles. These are related issue appearances; no independent family identity follows. <ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/979338930/ The Western Flying Post; or, Sherborne and Yeovil Mercury (The Sherborne Mercury, or Weekly Advertiser), 1746-06-30, p.2], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1334222061/ S Gravenhaegse Courant, 1746-09-21, p.1], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/979339079/ The Western Flying Post; or, Sherborne and Yeovil Mercury, 1746-11-17, p.2], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971385255/ The Gloucester Journal, 1746-11-18, p.2], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1334158733/ Opregte Haarlemsche Courant, 1746-12-01, p.1], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref>

The Gloucester Journal of 28 April 1747 describes Major Glascoe as lately discharged at London and chief major in Lord Ogilvy’s projected regiment. Nicholas is a probable contextual candidate; no forename is given, and English pay is not interpreted as British military service.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/971516263/ Gloucester Journal, 28 April 1747, p.1], original passage inspected 5 October 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The rare full name, Southwark proceedings and Hazard episode support a probable association across the 1746 reports. French birth and service are reported defence evidence. They do not establish an Irish origin, a Glasgow-family connection or relatives. The May 1747 appointment lacks a forename.

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
George Glasgow appears among Royal Artillery colonels in June 1811.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050144942/ Freeman’s Journal, 10 June 1811, p. 4], original previously inspected on 4 October 2026.</ref> A War Office notice in September 1819 lists Major-General George Glasgow of the Royal Artillery among officers taking lieutenant-general rank by brevet.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050057308/ Freeman’s Journal, 6 September 1819, p. 4], original previously inspected on 4 October 2026.</ref>

John W. Spurr’s biography records his appointment as an artillery cadet on 2 April 1771, colonel in 1806, major-general in July 1811 and lieutenant-general in August 1819. It gives his death as 28 October 1820 in London and names his late wife Margaret Green.<ref>[https://www.biographi.ca/en/bio/glasgow_george_5E.html John W. Spurr, “GLASGOW, GEORGE,” Dictionary of Canadian Biography, vol. 5], full English entry read on 17 October 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

The full DCB entry, successfully read through urllib on 17 October, identifies a cadet appointed 2 April 1771, colonel from 24 July 1806, major-general from 4 July 1811, lieutenant-general in August 1819, died 28 October 1820. This joins the June 1811 colonel and September 1819 brevet notices. Actual candidate biographies exclude 1529 (baptised 1769, aged two at cadet appointment), 3611 (born 1777, died 1857) and 3345 (born 1792). Retain the documented 6 October fully paged George/variant duplicate audit; no compatible profile found. Earlier 1771 first-lieutenant evidence describes another officer and must not be conflated with this 1771 cadet.

== Biography ==
On 10 March 1841, a Repeal Association entry reads “From Baddinstown, county Meath, per Mr. Owen Glasco, 1l.” and states that Mr. Glasco was admitted a member. On 25 February 1843, Owen Glasco appears among members “having each collected 20 Repealers”; the list ends with “Raddinstown County Meath.” The uncommon full name, association roles and Meath place context support probable continuity, but the 1843 list layout does not securely attach Raddinstown specifically to Owen. Retain the separate Baddinstown/Raddinstown readings; no modern place is identified. Neither notice proves birth, kinship or residence. “1l.” is £1; “20 Repealers” counts people collected, not money.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050131561/ Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1841-03-10, p.3]</ref><ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1050126480/ Freeman's Journal and Daily Commercial Advertiser, 1843-02-25, p.4]</ref>

== Research Notes ==

Glass-5334 (born 1840) and Glasgow-1954 (born 1846) cannot be the 1841 adult. Retain one probable 1841/1843 documentary Owen; keep Baddinstown/Raddinstown readings separate and do not invent a residence or family.

new_people.name: Bessie Glasgow, Quothquan executrix
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
'''Bessie Glasgow''' lived at Quodquen, now Quothquan in Lanarkshire, in 1650. She was the lawful sister of [[Glasgow-3296|John Glasgow]], whose testament dative and inventory were confirmed at Lanark on 27 May 1650. The opening calls Bessie his lawful sister; the confirmation calls the deceased John her brother and identifies her as his executrix dative.<ref name="Quothquan1650">National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court, testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow in Quodquen, confirmed 27 May 1650, CC14/5/5, register images 65–66; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills Scotland's People wills search]. The sibling clauses and continuity of both images were visually checked in the maintained original-image review of 10 September 2026; the full opening and accounts are not yet completely transcribed.</ref><ref>Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Lanark: Register of Testaments, 1595–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1903), printed p. 38, “Glasgow, John, in Quodquen,” 27 May 1650, [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/the_commissariot_record_of_lanark__register_of_testaments__1595-1800_~_1903.pdf#page=50 digital copy, PDF p. 50]. The calendar confirms John's estate entry; the original supplies Bessie's relationship.</ref>

Bessie was alive at that confirmation and was born before 1650. No age, birthplace, death date, spouse or child has been established. Quothquan is her recorded residence, not an established birthplace or death place.<ref name="Quothquan1650" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Family and identity ===
The two sibling clauses support the record-defined John–Bessie relationship at '''99% subjective confidence'''; they belong to one testament, not two independent sources. Bessie's identity among existing profiles remains unresolved. Compatible candidates include [[Glasgow-3361|Bessie Glasgow of South Leith, indexed in 1616]], [[Glasgow-1091|Elizabeth Glasgow of Glasgow, baptised in 1616]], [[Glasgow-1092|Bessie Glasgow of Glasgow, indexed in 1623]] and [[Glasgow-1517|Elizabeth Glasgow of Glasgow, christened in 1625]]. No baptism or later household is assigned to this woman merely from the shared name.

[[Glasgow-1029|Stephen Glasgow]] is the selected uncertain father of Bessie's brother John, assessed at '''22% subjective probability'''. Extending that same paternal hypothesis to the documented sister gives Bessie a '''conditional 22%''' placement. Stephen's adult Glasgow life in 1575 and marriage to [[Graham-38221|Margaret Grahame]] in 1582 permit the proposed generation, but do not connect that household to the Quothquan siblings.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 7, protocol 2189, printed p. 110, 17 June 1575, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n126/mode/2up digital copy]; vol. 8, protocol 2431, 25 June 1582, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsofproto08glas/page/56/mode/2up digital copy]. These name Stephen's parents and spouse, respectively, not Bessie or the Quothquan John as his children.</ref> This placement is dependent on John's hypothesis and adds no independent evidence for Stephen's paternity. Bessie's mother remains unknown; Margaret Grahame is not thereby her mother. No candidate baptism profile's documented parentage is changed by this conditional model.

Bessie Glasgow must be distinguished from [[Robertson-33965|Bessie Robertson]], the deceased spouse of a John Glasgow in Montfoid whose testament was confirmed in 1610.<ref>Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1901), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/n435/mode/1up p. 426], Robertson, Bessie, 17 August 1610; cross-reference under Glasgow, John, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/196/mode/1up p. 196].</ref> The Montfoid husband's identity with the Quothquan deceased is itself uncertain.

=== Existing-profile comparison ===

The checked candidates below are unselected. Sparse later lives are not exclusions.

{| class="wikitable"
! Candidate !! Evidence and disposition
|-
 | [[Glasgow-3361|Bessie Glasgow-3361]] || South Leith child indexed 25 February 1616, daughter of William Glasgow and Catherine Fraser; FamilySearch FQM4-VMQ. Age about 34 in 1650 is compatible. No later record in her biography excludes Quothquan. Retain as a compatible candidate; the different recorded father would displace the Stephen hypothesis if identity were established.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-1091|Elizabeth Glasgow-1091]] || Glasgow baptism, 15 December 1616, Robert Glasgow/Jonet Conynghame; OPR 644/1, 10/208. Compatible age about 33; no later-life contradiction. Retain, without treating name or age as an identity bridge.
|-

|-

|-

The approximate 1650 birth is unsupported by an age statement and does not exclude adulthood in 1650. Retain as a weaker candidate; no Scotland–Antrim identity is asserted.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-1155|Bessie Glasgow-1155]] || Inveresk index in March 1635; only about fifteen in May 1650. This strains the personal executor role and the proposed older sibling generation, but the combined birth/baptism index and absence of an inspected legal age clause do not justify a categorical exclusion. Retain as a substantially weaker candidate, without inventing an age cutoff.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-1161|Elizabeth Glasgow-1161]] || Edinburgh child account dated 1 July 1647, Thomas Glasgow/Catharine Weir. An infant baptism would make her only about three when the executrix appeared, a concrete chronological conflict with personal estate administration. However, the combined index has no inspected age statement, so retain this as a very weak candidate pending the original rather than turn an assumed infant baptism into a categorical exclusion.
|-
 | [[Glasgow-3915|Elizabeth Glasgow-3915]] || Already a widow occupying Easter Corswood in 1552, 98 years before the executrix's appearance. Exclude on the documented adult chronology, not her estimated 1525 birth.
|-

|-

None supplies a Glasgow birth surname or the Quothquan brother. They are weak unselected surname/household leads, not established contradictions or selected identities.

new_people.name: John Glasgow/Glasco, Prescott watchmaker
new_people.draft_wikitext:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
Reviewed: 2026-10-18. The documents establish a John Glasgow/Glasco of Prescott, watchmaker, as the brother-beneficiary named in Robert Glasgow's will and the grantor in B13. His identification with any existing John Glasgow profile is unresolved. Retain all six checked comparisons; none is selected or excluded by migration alone.

== Profile fields and identity hold ==

* First name: John; last name at birth: Glasgow (record spelling varies Glasgow/Glasco); male.
* Birth and death: unknown. The first known dated appearance is the will of 9 October 1849; this is not a birth-year estimate. Alive and conveying land on 30 October 1856.
* Birthplace and death place: unknown. Recorded residence: Prescott, Canada West (now Ontario), in 1856. Occupation in B13: watchmaker.
* Wife: Jane, releasing dower in B13; surname and further identity unknown.
* Brother: [[Glasgow-4150|Robert Glasgow of Prescott]], identified by the will and matched deed share.

=== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''', also recorded as John Glasco, was a brother of [[Glasgow-4150|Robert Glasgow of Prescott]], Canada West. Robert's will, dated 9 October 1849, gives one sixth of his estate to his brother John. The same will names brothers Daniel, Samuel and Thomas, sister Mary, and the children of brother James as beneficiaries.<ref name="will">Robert Glasgow of Prescott, will dated 9 October 1849, registered 13 November 1856, Prescott land registry, volume B, instrument B12, printed pp. 9–10, images 35–36; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S FamilySearch image 35], [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 image 36]. The original clauses and date line were visually inspected 18 October 2026.</ref>

On 30 October 1856, John Glasgow/Glasco of Prescott, described as a watchmaker, and his wife Jane conveyed their one-sixth interest to Samuel Glasgow, Prescott merchant, for £125. Jane released her dower interest. The conveyance covers Town Lot 12 on the south side of Dibble Street and part of Lot 11, a 3,400-square-foot strip. The deed was registered 13 November 1856.<ref name="b13">Indenture B13, dated 30 October 1856, registered 13 November 1856, Prescott land registry, volume B, printed pp. 10–11, image 36; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 FamilySearch image 36]. Original instrument visually inspected 18 October 2026.</ref>

The records establish his Prescott residence and watchmaking occupation by 1856. They do not establish his birth date or place, death, parents, or Jane's surname.

== Research Notes ==

The identification of the will's brother-beneficiary with B13's grantor is '''strongly supported (98% subjective confidence)''': the deed transfers exactly the one-sixth share allocated to John in the will, in the same Prescott property, seven years later. The will's registration request was witnessed by Alexander Glasgow; his role was witness, not beneficiary.<ref name="will" /><ref name="b13" />

[[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow-3904]] is the same tentative father hypothesis used for the related Prescott brothers Thomas, Daniel, Samuel and Robert. Extending that existing hypothesis to John is assessed at '''27%''', uncertain. It is not independent support for Alexander's paternity and must not raise the existing estimate. No mother is inferred. The will names no parents.

No existing John profile is selected. All six comparisons above remain open because an earlier or later residence elsewhere does not establish incompatible identity for a possible migrant. Further linking evidence could come from Canadian vital, religious, occupational or property records connecting a candidate's spouse/household to Jane and the Prescott share.

The 2007 online discussion supplies the derivative tradition naming Alexander and Rosanna as Thomas Glasgow’s parents, not a newly inspected record; it is retained as context only and does not establish this identity.<ref>“Glasgow Family,” Genes Reunited discussion board, 2007, https://www.genesreunited.co.uk/boards/board/general_topics/thread/465937 (prior review reused; not freshly inspected for this draft).</ref>

== Sources ==

<references />
new_people.assessment: John Glasgow, Prescott watchmaker with wife Jane in deed B13, is selected as Robert Glasgow-4150’s brother at 98% subjective confidence. Robert’s 1849 will gives brother John one sixth. John and Jane’s 1856 deed transfers an undivided one sixth of the same Dibble Street lots to Samuel, who is another will-named brother. The exact locality, buyer, parcels and fraction identify the grantor strongly; B13 does not itself expressly call John Robert’s brother. John’s birth, death and parents are not named, and his identity with an existing John profile is unresolved. Extend the existing Alexander Glasgow-3904 father hypothesis to John and Mary at 27%, uncertain, conditional on their documented membership in the Prescott sibling family. Thomas-987 and Daniel-3896 already carry this father, and Samuel-4010 and Robert-4150 already have the same selected uncertain hypothesis. Its basis remains the single late descendant tradition naming Alexander as Thomas’s father, with compatible generation and sibling inference. The original will and deeds name no parent. These two extensions supply no independent parent testimony and do not raise the existing estimate; no mother is selected. These are two previously unstructured record accounts recovered from evidence already researched in September, not two newly discovered sources or two proven additional distinct people. John retains six unselected compatible or weak existing-profile comparisons; later residence, spouse or death elsewhere is not by itself an exclusion of a possible migrant. No Mary Black/Glasgow match is established in the bounded local historical catalogue check. Both accounts remain on identity hold before any new WikiTree profile creation.
